name: Trinidad and Tobago

facts.religion: Christian about 55%, Hindu about 18%, Muslim about 5%

snapshot: The Caribbean's energy powerhouse, under a state of emergency over gang violence since March 2026, led by a prime minister closely aligned with Washington on Venezuela.
culture: Trinidad's Carnival is one of the world's great festivals, with calypso, soca and masquerade bands. The steelpan, made from oil drums in the 1930s, is the national instrument. Indo-Trinidadians, descended from indentured labourers, have made chutney music, Diwali and Phagwah part of national life. Cricket and Brian Lara are sources of pride.
society: Oil, gas and petrochemicals have made the country relatively wealthy, though output is declining. Gang violence has driven murders to record highs, prompting states of emergency. Politics largely splits between the Afro-Trinidadian-backed PNM and the Indo-Trinidadian-backed UNC.
situation: Kamla Persad-Bissessar's United National Congress won the April 2025 election, returning her to the job she held from 2010 to 2015. She has aligned closely with the Trump administration on Venezuela, though she said Trinidad took no part in the January 2026 raid that seized Maduro. In March 2026 her government declared a new state of emergency over persistent violent crime and later extended it.
power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the majority in the 41-seat House of Representatives; the president is elected by parliament and largely ceremonial. Tobago has its own House of Assembly.
